channel.title: Japan AI Monitor
channel.description: AI monitoring of Japan's political, economic and security developments

item.title: Proposals on reforming Prime Minister’s Office focus on leader’s time management
item.description: An LDP official cited the report, which compared Japan's system with other countries, to argue Japan's parliament demands more of its leader's time.

item.title: GIC acquires 16 Marriott-run hotels in Japan amid tourism boom
item.description: In the latest big real estate deal in Japan, Singapore's GIC took over Four Points Flex by Sheraton, a mid-price-range hotel chain.

item.title: Japan’s health cost caps rise, widening gaps between insurers
item.description: Japan's health care system is often held up abroad as a model of universal coverage, but universal does not mean uniform.

item.title: Japan’s output falls for second month due to impact from quake and Iran war
item.description: Wednesday's data suggest Japanese manufacturers may be feeling the impact of a major quake that hit Kyushu and the Iran war.

item.title: Igarashi and Ikeda clinch surfing gold at Asian Games
item.description: Japan also secured another medal in surfing, with Minami Nonaka securing bronze in the women's shortboard event.

item.title: Settler attack on West Bank village injures Israeli forces, drawing rare rebuke
item.description: The raid came amid mounting international criticism of settler violence, which Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu downplayed last week.

item.title: Japan lifts sanctions on 16 entities linked to Syria
item.description: Since the collapse of the Assad regime in 2024, Tokyo has eased its sanctions in light of steps taken by Syria's new government.

item.title: ‘Like a jewel’: Japan’s luxury ice revered by bars worldwide
item.description: The luxury product, believed to melt more slowly than regular ice, is painstakingly shaped by craftsmen in Kanazawa.

item.title: Toyota eyes selling Japan’s answer to Rolls-Royce around the world
item.description: With global interest in all things Japan surging, Toyota has reasons to be confident the Century can be successful overseas.

item.title: U.K.’s Burnham restores some hope, but near-term fixes prove elusive
item.description: It remains unclear when Prime Minister Andy Burnham will plot a detailed route to become the "circuit-breaker" for Britain's political instability.

item.title: Japan’s new arctic research vessel set to arrive in December
item.description: Mirai II will replace the 8,700-ton Mirai, which was decommissioned in December last year.

item.title: Price hikes to hit Japanese households starting next month
item.description: Households will likely feel an increased financial burden, given that price hikes will also hit a wide range of food products.

item.title: Japan’s population fell 2.5% between 2020 and 2025, census shows
item.description: This was the third consecutive decline in the five-year survey that dates back to 1920.

item.title: Man held on suspicion of giving information to tokuryū criminal group
item.description: The arrest is believed to be the first by the Tokyo police of a suspected information source in connection with crimes involving tokuryū groups.

item.title: Swiss franc, Japanese yen Rise as DeepSeek News Boosts Safe Havens
item.description: The Yen and Swiss Franc were stronger against the dollar as investors sought safe havens after Chinese start-up DeepSeek’s new AI model hit U.S. tech stocks.
